name: Gargi Saha

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Gargi Saha is a poet whose collections include The Muse in My Salad Days (2000) and Letters to Him (2012). Reviewing the latter, Ramesh Anand describes its linked poems as an extended dialogue of prayer, questioning and gratitude. Her poetry has also appeared in Literary Vibes.

Her Kabita Live contributions find expressive possibilities in everyday sights and sounds. ‘Onomatopoeia’ gathers a world of rustling, humming and calls, while ‘The Simple Pleasures of Life’ attends to birds, rain and green landscapes. ‘Ineffable Altruism’ asks what people owe the earth that feeds them; ‘Withdrawal’ turns towards isolation and remembered happiness. These contrasting poems place delight beside vulnerability.
